samples.summary: Round-trip unset of `dp` on currency/percent formats *increases* the displayed decimals, because an absent `dp` means the format's default (2), not the value's own precision
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` decides to restore inheritance when `target === valueDp` (sheet.ts:4212) and then removes only `dp` for any format that is not `'number'` (`const values = nf === 'number' ? { dp, nf } : { dp }`, line 4219-4220). But `formatValue` falls back to `decimals = dp ?? 2` (format.ts:119) / the currency default when `dp` is undefined — it does NOT render `valueDp`. Concrete: cell A1 = `1234` with style `{nf:'currency', cu:'USD', dp:0}` (exactly what the xlsx importer writes, xlsx-styles.ts:236). Increase decimals → explicit `dp:1`. Decrease decimals → dp=1, valueDp=0, target=0===valueDp, selectionRendersAt(0) is true → `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp:1})` removes `dp` → the cell now renders `$1,234.00` (2 decimals) instead of `$1,234`. Pressing *decrease* decimals made the display gain two decimals, and the original dp:0 formatting is lost. The same holds for `nf:'percent'`. The `target === valueDp` guard is only sound for plain/`'number'`-without-nf rendering.

samples.summary: Increase/decrease decimals silently deletes a user-chosen `nf: 'number'` format (and its thousands grouping) whenever the stepped dp happens to equal the value's own precision
samples.evidence: When `nf === 'number'` the unset request is `{ dp, nf }` (sheet.ts:4219-4220), i.e. the number format itself is removed. The code cannot distinguish an `nf:'number'` the user chose from one a previous step added. Example: A1 = `1234.5` with `{nf:'number', dp:0}` (grouped, no decimals — a state a user reaches with the toolbar or that the importer writes). Click *increase* decimals: dp=0, valueDp=1, target=1===valueDp, selectionRendersAt(1) true → `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp:0, nf:'number'})` strips both keys → display goes from `1,234` to `1234.5`, i.e. the grouping/number format the user chose is destroyed by an increase-decimals click. The existing test 'should keep a number format the user chose' only covers the case where valueDp differs from the target, so this path is untested.

samples.summary: Decrease decimals becomes a silent no-op for a multi-cell selection whenever the active cell has no explicit dp, even though other selected cells have decimals to drop
samples.evidence: `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp) { return; }` (sheet.ts:4198-4202) is decided purely from the ACTIVE cell. Select A1:B1 where A1=`12` (no style → dp=0, explicitDp=false) and B1=`1.2345` (no style). Clicking decrease decimals now returns before touching anything, so B1 keeps 4 decimals. The previous implementation (spreadsheet.ts, removed lines) wrote `{dp: Math.max(0, dp-1), nf:'number'}` over the whole selection, so B1 went to 0 decimals. The new test 'should keep stepping a selection whose active cell is already at zero' only exercises the case where the active cell has an *explicit* dp:0 (the `clamped` branch), so this regression is uncovered.

samples.summary: Unsetting the last keys of a sheet/column/row style persists an empty `{}` style layer, so `resolveEffectiveStyle`/`getStyle` start returning a truthy empty object for every cell instead of `undefined`
samples.evidence: `omitStyleKeys` can return `{}` (range-styles.ts:71-75 — it only returns undefined when *no* key is present). The sheet/col/row branches then store it verbatim (`await this.store.setSheetStyle(next)`, sheet.ts:4395; same for columns 4407 and rows 4420) and MemStore/Yorkie keep it as-is (memory.ts:408). `resolveEffectiveStyle` short-circuits to undefined only when every layer is falsy (`if (!s && !c && !r && !range && !cellStyle) return undefined`, sheet.ts:883), so a leftover `{}` sheetStyle makes `getStyle` return `{}` for the whole sheet after a whole-sheet increase+decrease round trip. The new tests for the sheet/column/row round trips assert only `style?.dp === undefined`, which passes with the stale empty layer. Downstream `if (style)` consumers (e.g. frontend activeCellStyle null-checks) can observe the difference.

samples.summary: `compactCell` now preserves spill metadata, but `isEmptyCell` still ignores it, so a style-only rewrite can delete a spill ghost cell whose value is empty
samples.evidence: The diff deliberately carries `spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked` through `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:69-80) so a style-only rewrite does not detach a ghost. `isEmptyCell` (style-mutation.ts:48-52) was not updated: it looks only at v/f/s, and `hasCellContent` treats `v === ''` as no content. Ghost cells are written as `{ v: values[dr]?.[dc] ?? '', spillAnchor: sref }` (calculator.ts:141), so a ghost with an empty spilled value plus a dp/nf style hits `unsetRangeStyleValues`' delete branch (`if (isEmptyCell(nextCell)) await this.store.delete(anchor)`, sheet.ts:4448-4449) and the spillAnchor the change just took care to preserve is dropped. `clearCellStylesInRange` (sheet.ts:2007-2012) reaches the same branch.

samples.summary: `unsetRangeStyleValues` performs one awaited `store.get` per populated cell of the selection, on top of a full grid scan in `selectionRendersAt` — a whole-sheet decrease-decimals walks the entire used range twice
samples.evidence: `selectionRendersAt` fetches the grid for every selection range (sheet.ts:4244) and `unsetRangeStyleValues` fetches it again (4360) and then awaits `this.store.get(anchor)` for each entry (4369). For `selectAllCells()` the target is the full dimension range, so a sheet with hundreds of thousands of populated cells does that many awaited store reads on the UI path before a single write; the previous implementation was a single `setRangeStyle` writing one sheet-level style. No cap is applied here, unlike other whole-selection operations which are bounded (`MaxBorderSelectionCells`, `MaxCheckboxToggleCells`, sheet.ts:140-143).

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` counts characters after the first '.', so scientific notation and text are measured wrongly and can drive `dp` past Intl's limit
samples.evidence: `decimalsInValue('1.5e+30')` returns 5 (it counts `5e+30`), and `decimalsInValue('a.bcdefg')` returns 7 for text. That number is used both as the inferred starting dp (sheet.ts:4183) and as the round-trip equality test across the whole selection (`selectionRendersAt`, sheet.ts:4251), so a value in exponent form both starts from the wrong precision and can never agree with the format's real precision. With a long literal decimal (e.g. `0.` + 150 digits, a legal stored value) the inferred dp exceeds Intl's `maximumFractionDigits` range and `safeFormat` re-throws in its own catch (format.ts:14-18, the retry uses the same offending options), which would surface as an uncaught RangeError during render.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim: sheet.ts:4219-4220 builds the unset request as `{ dp, nf }` whenever `nf === 'number'`, and the gate at 4209-4214 (`explicitDp && !clamped && target === valueDp && selectionRendersAt(target)`) cannot tell a user/importer-chosen `nf:'number'` from one a previous step added. unsetRangeStyleValues' verdictFor (4310-4325) returns 'match' for a layer holding both `dp:0` and `nf:'number'` and omitStyleKeys (4380) strips both keys, so the number format really is destroyed. The state is reachable two ways: (1) the XLSX importer emits `{nf:'number', dp:0}` for the grouped `#,##0` family (xlsx-styles.ts:227,232,246,265), so a cell holding `1234.5` loses grouping on a single increase-decimals click; (2) toolbar-only path — formatting-toolbar.tsx:243 applies `{nf:'number'}` with no dp, then two decreases reach `{nf:'number',dp:0}` and the next increase unsets both, leaving the cell with no format at all, which also violates the round-trip invariant the method's own comment (4189-4193) states. The existing tests miss this: decimals.test.ts:366-382 uses value `1234` (valueDp=0) and only the clamped decrease; :384-398 covers `nf` with no `dp`. Real, reachable, silent loss of user-chosen formatting — squarely in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Decrease decimals becomes a silent no-op for a multi-cell selection whenever the active cell has no explicit dp, even though other selected cells have decimals to drop
finding.evidence: `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp) { return; }` (sheet.ts:4198-4202) is decided purely from the ACTIVE cell. Select A1:B1 where A1=`12` (no style → dp=0, explicitDp=false) and B1=`1.2345` (no style). Clicking decrease decimals now returns before touching anything, so B1 keeps 4 decimals. The previous implementation (spreadsheet.ts, removed lines) wrote `{dp: Math.max(0, dp-1), nf:'number'}` over the whole selection, so B1 went to 0 decimals. The new test 'should keep stepping a selection whose active cell is already at zero' only exercises the case where the active cell has an *explicit* dp:0 (the `clamped` branch), so this regression is uncovered.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. sheet.ts:4196-4202 derives `dp`/`explicitDp` solely from the active cell via getActiveDecimalState (sheet.ts:4165-4186), then returns early when `stepped < 0 && !explicitDp`, before selectionTargets() (sheet.ts:4263-4267) or any write is reached. For A1=`12` with no style, getActiveDecimalState returns dp=0/explicitDp=false (branch at sheet.ts:4182-4184), so Decrease on selection A1:B1 is a total no-op and B1=`1.2345` keeps 4 decimals; spreadsheet.ts:544-548 calls straight into this with no compensating logic. The claimed test gap also holds: decimals.test.ts:104-117 sets an explicit {dp:0,nf:'number'} on the active cell, exercising only the `clamped` branch (sheet.ts:4206-4207), and decimals.test.ts:94-102 covers only a single empty cell. The behavior is documented as a deliberate deviation in docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:254-257 and docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:88-92, which is why my confidence on blocking is low — but documentation authored by the change under review is not a guard, does not make the path unreachable, and does not move a silent user-visible functional regression out of the correctness lane. No named refutation ground applies.

mergedFrom.summary: `removeCellStyleKeysInRange` rewrites cells through `compactCell`, dropping spill metadata
unsetRangeStyleValues returns true even when it removed nothing, so the caller reports success for a no-op

finding.summary: unsetRangeStyleValues treats a missing key as agreement, so a cell that carries only some of the requested keys loses the rest
finding.evidence: The conflict scan is `if (cellValue !== undefined && cellValue !== value) return false;` (sheet.ts:4306-4310), but the removal is `omitStyleKeys(existing.s, keys)` — it strips *all* requested keys regardless of which ones the cell actually agreed about. changeDecimals calls it with `{dp, nf:'number'}` (sheet.ts:4208-4210). Scenario: A1 = `12` with `{dp:1, nf:'number'}`, B1 = `12` with `{nf:'number'}` only (no dp). Select A1:B1, press decrease → target 0 === valueDp 0, so unset `{dp:1, nf:'number'}` runs. B1's `nf` matches and its `dp` is undefined, so no conflict is detected; B1 then has both keys omitted and ends up with no style at all, changing its render from `12.00` to `12`. The same asymmetry applies to the col/row/sheet/patch layer checks (sheet.ts:4258-4285), where a layer holding only `nf` and no `dp` is silently accepted and then stripped. The added tests only cover the case where the other cell *disagrees* about a value (currency, dp:5), never the case where it holds a strict subset of the keys.

verdict.reason: The finding rests on a quoted conflict scan (`if (cellValue !== undefined && cellValue !== value) return false;`) that does not exist in sheet.ts — that literal appears only in unrelated predicates (filter.ts:20, conditional-format.ts:45, yorkie-store.ts:129). The real implementation is `verdictFor` at sheet.ts:4310-4325, which counts how many requested keys a layer holds and returns 'conflict' when `held !== entries.length` (sheet.ts:4324) — exactly the partial-subset guard the finding says is missing. Running the finding's own scenario: for entries [dp, nf] against B1's `{nf:'number'}`, dp is undefined so it is skipped, nf matches so held=1, and 1 !== 2 yields 'conflict'; the cell loop at sheet.ts:4373-4376 then returns false before any write, and changeDecimals falls through to the explicit setRangeStyle path (sheet.ts:4221-4230). Nothing is stripped. The col/row/sheet/patch layers use the same verdictFor through `refuses` (sheet.ts:4328-4353), so the claimed layer-level asymmetry is absent as well; omitStyleKeys (range-styles.ts:64-76) is only reached after a 'match' verdict. The claim that tests never cover the subset case is also false: decimals.test.ts:384-398 covers precisely a cell carrying nf with no dp and asserts the format survives.

finding.summary: Decrease/increase decimals can change other cells' displayed precision because the unset decision uses only the active cell's `valueDp`
finding.evidence: `const { dp, nf, valueDp, explicitDp } = await this.getActiveDecimalState()` (4196) and `if (explicitDp && target === valueDp && inheritable)` (4203) test the ACTIVE cell's raw-value precision but the resulting unset applies to the whole selection. Concretely: A1='1.5', A2='1.2345', select A1:A2. Decrease → writes {dp:0, nf:'number'} for both (shows 2 / 1). Increase → dp=0 explicit, target 1 === valueDp(A1)=1, nf='number' → all dp/nf removed → A1 renders '1.5' (intended) but A2 jumps back to '1.2345', i.e. pressing *increase by one decimal* moved A2 from 0 to 4 decimals. The old code wrote an explicit uniform dp and had no such divergence.

verdict.reason: The unset branch is not decided by the active cell's `valueDp` alone: `sheet.ts:4209-4214` requires `await this.selectionRendersAt(target)` in addition to `explicitDp && !clamped && target === valueDp`. `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4242-4257) iterates every range of the selection (`selectionTargets`, sheet.ts:4263-4267) and returns false if any numeric cell's `decimalsInValue(value)` differs from the target, so a selection that disagrees about precision falls through to the explicit `{dp: target}` write at sheet.ts:4226-4230. Replaying the reviewer's exact case (A1='1.5', A2='1.2345', select A1:A2): on increase, `decimalsInValue('1.2345')=4 !== 1` (format.ts:92-98) makes the guard return false, so no dp/nf is removed and A2 renders at 1 decimal — not the claimed jump back to 4 decimals. The scenario is also covered by an existing test asserting the guarded behavior (decimals.test.ts:400-418).

finding.summary: Comment/assumption that dropping `nf:'number'` keeps the cell looking the same is false — grouping separators are lost
finding.evidence: Lines 4204-4207 justify removing `nf` with "the cell keeps looking the same", but `formatValue(value,'number',dp)` goes through `toLocaleString` (format.ts:127-130) which adds thousands separators, while plain format returns the raw string verbatim (format.ts:111-113). For value '1234.5': with {nf:'number',dp:1} the cell shows '1,234.5'; after the unset it shows '1234.5'. The new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:89-92 encodes exactly this lossy outcome (`toBe('1234.5')`). So decrease-then-increase on a number-formatted cell silently drops the user's number format and its grouping.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted comment is misattributed — no "the cell keeps looking the same" text exists (sheet.ts:4203-4206 is about the clamp; the real comment at sheet.ts:4215-4218 openly admits "That gives up the grouping separators it added too ('1,234.5' → '1234.5')"). However, the substantive claim — that decrease-then-increase silently drops a number-formatted cell's nf and its grouping — is real and reachable on a user-chosen format, so it cannot be refuted. Trace: cell value '1234.56' with a user-set {nf:'number'} and no dp; getActiveDecimalState (sheet.ts:4182-4185) returns dp=2, explicitDp=false, so the decrease skips the unset branch (guarded by explicitDp at sheet.ts:4209-4211) and writes {dp:1}, which merges into the same tail range patch (sheet.ts:1873-1902), yielding one layer {nf:'number', dp:1}. The following increase now has explicitDp=true, stepped=2 === valueDp=2 and selectionRendersAt(2) true, so sheet.ts:4219-4221 requests unset of {dp:1, nf:'number'}; verdictFor returns 'match' for that merged layer (sheet.ts:4316-4324) and it is owned (sheet.ts:4348-4353), so both keys are removed. The cell permanently loses the number format the user chose, rendering '1234.56' instead of '1,234.56' (formatValue: format.ts:111-113 vs 124-131). The existing regression test "should keep a number format the user chose" (decimals.test.ts:156-175) does not cover this because its value '12' has valueDp=0, which never equals the stepped target. Loss of user-set state on a normal toolbar interaction is a major correctness defect.
